home.title: 中華そば 麦の星 MUGI no HOSHI｜House-made noodle ramen in Nagoya
home.description: A ramen shop built around noodles made in our own noodle room. 1 min from Shinsakae-machi Station, Nagoya. Tabelog Ramen Hyakumeiten 2025.

menu.title: Menu｜中華そば 麦の星 MUGI no HOSHI
menu.description: Shio and shoyu chuka soba, back-fat noodles, kombu-water tsukemen, oi-soba, rice dishes and more. All prices include tax.

concept.title: Our noodles｜中華そば 麦の星 MUGI no HOSHI
concept.description: We make the noodles first, from Japanese wheat, then choose the soup and the way to eat them. This is what we call Mugi-kei.

home.heroSub: House-made noodle ramen, 1 min from Shinsakae-machi Station
philosophyLines: We search for the finest noodles,
pair them with the right soup,
and create a bowl like no other.
Shock the world with ramen featuring noodles!
home.philosophyBody: We use wheat from many regions of Japan and make our noodles first, in the noodle room inside the shop. Then we choose the soup and the way to eat them to suit those noodles. We call this order Mugi-kei — “wheat style.”
home.signatureLead: Noodles, soup and toppings — every part of our signature bowl has been reworked.
home.oisobaBody: Oi-soba is a small bowl of mazesoba (soupless, sauced noodles). Unlike kaedama (extra plain noodles), it is already seasoned, so it is delicious on its own. You can also add it to the soup left in your chuka soba.
home.oisobaNote: The oi-soba noodles change from time to time: thin noodles with a crisp bite, flat noodles, green noodles made with spinach powder, and more.
howSteps: Buy a meal ticket at the ticket machine by the entrance first. Cash only.
Take your ticket and have a seat.
home.howNote: We do not take reservations. On days when a new dish is released, there may be a line outside.
home.vibeTitle: A ramen shop that feels like a café.
home.vibeBody: A white sign, a mustard-yellow entrance and warm string lights. Inside, a light wooden counter and clean, bright walls. Unusually for a ramen shop, about 40% of our guests are women. Feel free to drop in on your own.
manifesto: A never-ending path of noodle making.

menu.title: Menu

menu.oisobaNote: Oi-soba is a small, seasoned mazesoba. Kaedama is an extra serving of plain, unseasoned noodles.

concept.title: Our noodles
concept.lead: A will to master noodles. A never-ending path of noodle making.

sections.title: Ramen that starts with the noodles
sections.body: At MUGI no HOSHI, every bowl starts with the noodles. We make them from carefully chosen wheat from many regions of Japan, then look for the soup and the way of eating that suit those noodles best. We call this style Mugi-kei.

sections.title: Our noodle room
sections.body: Our noodles are made in the noodle room at the back of the shop. You can see into it through a window from the dining area.

sections.title: Seafood broth for shio, chicken broth for shoyu
sections.body: Our signature chuka soba comes in two kinds. The shio (salt) soup is made with seafood broth, and the shoyu (soy sauce) soup with chicken broth. Each is paired with its own noodles.

sections.title: One more kind of noodle with oi-soba
sections.body: The oi-soba noodles change from time to time: thin noodles, flat noodles, green noodles made with spinach. Enjoying a different noodle after your bowl of chuka soba is something only a noodle-making shop can offer.

access.title: Access
access.lead: 1 min walk from Exit 2 of Shinsakae-machi Station on the Higashiyama Subway Line.
directions: Get off at Shinsakae-machi Station on the Higashiyama Subway Line and take Exit 2.
The shop is about 110 m (1 min) from Exit 2. Look for the yellow entrance and the lit-up “MUGI no HOSHI” sign.

photoAlts.entrance: The yellow entrance with the MUGI no HOSHI sign
photoAlts.exterior: The shop front, lit by string lights

items.a: No. We do not take reservations. Guests are seated in order of arrival.

items.q: Is it easy to visit on my own?
items.a: Yes. The shop is bright and café-like, and about 40% of our guests are women. We have both counter and table seats.
Cash only. Please buy a meal ticket at the ticket machine by the entrance first. Credit cards, e-money and QR code payments are not accepted.
Buy a meal ticket at the ticket machine by the entrance, then take a seat.

items.q: What is the difference between oi-soba and kaedama?
items.a: Oi-soba is a small, seasoned mazesoba. You can eat it as it is, or add it to the soup left in your chuka soba. Kaedama is an extra serving of plain, unseasoned noodles.

items.q: It's my first visit. What do you recommend?
items.a: We recommend the Chuka Soba Shio most of all: seafood broth with our house-made noodles.
On days when a new dish is released, there may be a line outside.
On Wednesdays. We also close on some other days (New Year, staff training, etc.) and announce them on Instagram in advance.

items.q: Is there a last order time?
items.a: No. We serve until closing time.

owner.title: From the owner
owner.name: Imamura, owner
owner.quote: I love ramen so much that I travel to popular shops in and outside Aichi just to eat. That love gives me all kinds of inspiration for creating new noodles. Nothing makes me happier than seeing guests enjoy a bowl I have put everything into.
